WELCOME

This report brings together perspectives from the people you work with most closely: your reporting manager, skip-level manager / BU Head (where applicable), peers, internal customers, direct reports, and your own self-assessment.

This feedback offers an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of how others experience your strengths, contributions, and opportunities for growth.

MAKING THE MOST OUT OF YOUR FEEDBACK
As you review this report:
  • Assume positive intent and view the feedback as an opportunity to learn.
  • Look for patterns and themes rather than focusing on individual comments.
  • Take time to reflect before drawing conclusions or deciding on actions.
  • Consider how the insights align with your experiences and aspirations.
SUPPORT AVAILABLE TO YOU
Your DC Coach will partner with you to:
  • Identify the key themes and messages emerging from the feedback.
  • Connect these insights to your current role, challenges, and aspirations.
  • Prioritise development areas and build a meaningful development plan.
This report will be shared with your manager and the HR team. Its purpose is developmental: to support meaningful conversations, focused growth, and sustained professional development.

03
COMPETENCY FRAMEWORK

Bajaj Auto's Leadership Competency Framework is built on the 4A model: Act, Adapt, Align, Anticipate. Together, these represent the leadership behaviours expected across all levels.

ACT: THE FOUNDATION

Act represents the execution mindset, ownership, and discipline that holds the other three As together. Because it shows up through how every other competency is demonstrated, Act is treated as a given in this feedback exercise rather than being assessed as a separate area.

ADAPT, ALIGN AND ANTICIPATE: WHAT IS MEASURED HERE
These three themes are demonstrated through the nine competencies in this report, grouped into four sections: Task & Execution, People & Relationships, Culture, and Strategy & Change.

To protect confidentiality, a group's score is shown only when there are at least 2 respondents in that group. Self, Reporting Manager, and Skip Manager / BU Head are exceptions: these always appear, even with one respondent.
A note on Skip Manager / BU Head ratings. Skip Manager / BU Head respondents complete a shorter version of the survey, containing 15 statements selected for their visibility into the Participant's behaviours at this level. Their scores are presented in the same tables as other respondent groups for ease of reading, but may not be directly comparable at the behaviour level since they reflect a smaller subset of statements.

How to read the Gap column
  • ↑ Possible blind spot: you rate yourself meaningfully higher than others do (gap ≥ 0.75). Worth a closer look.
  • ↓ Possible hidden strength: others rate you meaningfully higher than you rate yourself (gap ≥ 0.75). You may be underestimating your impact in this area.
  • No significant gap: your self-perception and others' perception are broadly aligned. While perceptions are consistent, both high and low scores can offer useful insights into areas to leverage, sustain, and further develop.
